newsitem.title: JAPAN: Volvo recalls 3,258 cars in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Volvo recalls 3,258 cars in Japan.

text.p: Volvo Cars Japan Corp, the Japanese unit of AB Volvo, said on Tuesday it had told the Transport Ministry it is recalling 3,258 Volvo cars due to engine and brake problems.
The defective Volvo 850 and 960 series cars were imported between September 27, 1992, and September 27 this year.
A screw in the throttle valve could lead to problems with engine revolutions and another defect concerns a traction control unit which could cause a decline in braking force.
Repair costs are estimated at 80,000 yen per car for replacing the traction control unit and 29,000 to 30,000 yen per car for the throttle valve problem, a Volvo Cars Japan spokesman said.
No accidents have been reported but the company has received four complaints in Japan, the spokesman said.
